source_text: Nam si universitatem, quam fecunditas humana protulit, regno diaboli peccatum naturale transcripsit et inde in extrema aetate mundi aliqui liberati per Christum putantur, quae veritas est aut quae auctoritas eius Magistri, qui contra tam clarum testimonium totius mundi dicit in plures iustitiam abundasse quam culpam? Quid ergo ei creditur de involutis dogmatibus disserenti, si de rebus tam perspicuis mentiatur? Quod quia sentire sacrilegium est, id autem dici dogma tuum compulit, honore Apostoli Manichaeorum vilitas conteratur.
pass_a_gloss: For if a natural sin transcribed to the devil's kingdom the universality which human fecundity brought forth, and from there in the last age of the world some are thought freed through Christ, what truth is there or what authority of that Teacher, who against so clear a testimony of the whole world says that justice abounded unto more than fault? Why therefore is he believed discussing involved dogmas, if he lies about things so perspicuous? Which because to mean it is a sacrilege, but your dogma compelled that to be said, let the cheapness of the Manichaeans be crushed by the honor of the Apostle.

lemmas.lexica: LS fecunditas; Blaise blessed fertility of marriage
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: If natural sin transferred to the devil’s kingdom everyone whom human fertility produced, and some are thought to have been freed from it through Christ in the world’s final age, what truth or authority belongs to that teacher who, against such clear evidence from the whole world, says righteousness abounded to more people than guilt? Why believe him when he discusses obscure doctrines, if he lies about things so obvious? But to think this is sacrilege, and it was your doctrine that forced it to be said. Let the apostle’s honor therefore crush the Manichaeans’ worthlessness (compare Romans 5:15) (Romans 5:15).

choices.why: God-blessed fertility of the first pair; Julian will not let Paul accuse it.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
